item.text:
**8B.9 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos (2024)**

Overall, the 2024 record is mixed but leans toward a regime-management reading: Marcos repeatedly tried to de-escalate the South China Sea crisis and preserve alliance leverage, while domestic opposition space remained constrained by red-tagging, media pressure, and selective accountability.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Title:** [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos-3492819) | **Publisher:** Reuters | **Date:** June 23, 2024 | **Claim:** Marcos publicly said the Philippines was not trying to start wars and would settle disputes peacefully, while also saying his forces would not use force or intimidation. This supports a restrained crisis-management style that still preserves territorial position and state credibility. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9, 2B.7

- **Title:** [China and Philippines reach tentative deal to defuse tensions at South China Sea flashpoint](https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jul/22/china-and-philippines-deal-south-china-sea-sierra-madre) | **Publisher:** Reuters | **Date:** July 21, 2024 | **Claim:** Manila and Beijing reached a provisional arrangement on resupply missions and framed it as de-escalation through dialogue and good-faith implementation. This is strong evidence that Marcos chose crisis management and channel preservation over open escalation. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9, 2B.7

- **Title:** [Philippines’ Marcos vows countermeasures in response to Chinese ‘attacks’](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-marcos-vows-countermeasures-in-response-to-chinese-attacks/2018365/) | **Publisher:** Reuters | **Date:** March 28, 2024 | **Claim:** Marcos threatened proportionate and reasonable countermeasures against Chinese coast-guard and maritime-militia pressure. This cuts the other way from pure restraint: he was willing to harden the state response to preserve sovereignty and deterrence. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9, 2B.7

- **Title:** [Philippines: Dangerous ‘Red Tagging’ of Labor Leaders](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders) | **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch | **Date:** September 25, 2024 | **Claim:** HRW reported that officials, police, and military personnel harassed union leaders through red-tagging, home visits, and threats, causing fear and union withdrawal. This is strong negative evidence on opposition/civil-society management. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9

- **Title:** [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | **Publisher:** Freedom House | **Date:** 2024 | **Claim:** Freedom House said elections remained formally open, but disinformation, vote buying, criminal cases against critics, and persistent red-tagging distorted competition and advantaged established elites. This is broad negative evidence that the political environment was not fully open or neutral. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9

- **Title:** [No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it – PBBM](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/) | **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office | **Date:** November 14, 2024 | **Claim:** Marcos refused cooperation with the ICC probe into Duterte’s drug war, while allowing only tightly controlled domestic review and preserving Interpol obligations. This shows selective openness to accountability and a clear limit on independent external scrutiny. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9

- **Title:** [Marcos on people’s initiative for Cha-cha: let Comelec do their job](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/) | **Publisher:** GMA News Online | **Date:** January 23, 2024 | **Claim:** Marcos told critics to let the election commission handle allegations of signature-buying rather than intervening directly. This is modest evidence of procedural restraint and some respect for institutional boundaries. | **Question IDs:** 8B.9

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a high-confidence 2024 source showing Marcos personally overrode the Supreme Court, dismantled opposition parties, or used a formal emergency crackdown against domestic rivals.
- The strongest negative evidence is indirect and environment-level: red-tagging, media pressure, politicized information space, and refusal of independent ICC scrutiny. That supports a coercive or selectively constrained system, but not a full emergency-authoritarian episode.
